windows.title: Run Windows apps
windows.about: Many Windows programs and games run on OrionOS. Bottles runs Windows programs, each in its own sandboxed bottle. Steam runs most Windows games with Proton. Lutris adds other game stores. Nothing here is installed unless you choose it.
windows.caution: Not everything works: games with strict anti-cheat (Valorant, League of Legends, Fortnite) and Adobe's apps don't. Check a program at protondb.com (games) or the Bottles and WineHQ app lists before you rely on it. Orion never ships Windows programs or game files: you bring your own.

apps.name: Bottles
apps.use: Windows programs: make a bottle (Application or Gaming), then add the program's installer or .exe.

apps.name: Steam
apps.use: Windows games: Steam > Settings > Compatibility > turn on Steam Play for all titles.

apps.name: Lutris
apps.use: Optional: Battle.net, EA, Ubisoft and other stores, with install scripts for many games.

recipes.name: WoW 1.12 on your own server
recipes.about: Your own 1.12 client folder (bring it from Windows with Move my stuff) in a Bottles bottle, with realmlist.wtf pointing at your server. No game files are downloaded or shipped.

recipes.name: Bring my Windows apps list
recipes.about: Reads the list Move my stuff made on Windows and offers the Linux version of each app.

studio.title: Orion Studio
studio.about: The Craft creative suite from the ArtCraft team (storytold on GitHub): free apps written in Rust that imitate well-known commercial tools, dual-licensed MIT / Apache-2.0. Optional: nothing here is installed unless you choose it.
studio.caution: Most of the suite is alpha or still in development; PhotoCraft's own README says it is not yet a replacement for daily professional work. The apps describe themselves as clean-room reimplementations. Some people have publicly questioned how they were made, and nothing is proven either way, so Orion only offers them from their official releases and never bundles them.
studio.how_to_install: These aren't on Flathub yet. Their official GitHub releases have a Flatpak bundle and an AppImage. Download the .flatpak and SHA256SUMS.txt into the same folder, then press Install downloaded file: Orion checks the checksum and that it's this app before installing.
